items.context: Phase 2 of the plan moves handlers/services into domain-aligned modules. The two realistic endpoints are (A) file-level grouping within the existing `api` package, or (B) real Go subpackages. Subpackages enforce boundaries at compile time but risk import cycles because the current flat package shares helpers freely (rate limiters, session managers, shared DTOs). The item description requires behavior-preserving changes with minimum risk.

options.label: File-level grouping within existing `api` package
options.rationale: Lowest-risk brownfield move. Gives us `RegisterRoutes` per domain, grouped deps structs, and visual domain separation without touching import paths or triggering cycles. Leaves the door open to escalate to subpackages in a follow-up.

options.label: Full Go subpackages (e.g., `api/domain/billing`)
options.rationale: Strongest boundary enforcement but very likely to expose import cycles through shared helpers; would balloon the diff and risk behavior drift during extraction.

options.label: Hybrid — subpackages for isolated domains, file-level for the rest
options.rationale: Compromise: split out domains with clean dep graphs (e.g., `ai`, `remote-profile`) and leave intertwined ones at file level. More judgment calls, more diff complexity.

items.context: `api/routes.go` currently registers 18 route groups. Refactoring 1:1 gives 18 domain modules — tidy per file but dilutes the 'screaming architecture' intent and creates thin modules (e.g., `credits`, `update`). Collapsing into ~8 cohesive domains (landing, billing[+credits+commerce-admin], downloads[+content+update], ai, metrics[+feedback+waitlist], admin[+admin-user+docs-admin], remote-profile, user-auth[+auth+account]) makes boundaries louder but requires judgment on where each current group belongs.

options.label: Collapse into 8 domain modules as proposed in the plan
options.rationale: Makes domain boundaries actually visible, matches the scenario's conceptual model (landing-page + business-suite + ai + user auth), and reduces file count. Requires the groupings below to be approved.

options.label: 1:1 with existing 18 `register*Routes` calls
options.rationale: Simplest mechanical transform and lowest grouping-judgment risk; but leaves the 'monolith of micro-files' shape and fails the 'scream your domain' goal.

items.context: `ui/src/App.tsx` currently mixes route definitions with providers. Phase 3 extracts routes into modules under `ui/src/app/routes/`. The question is the split: three surface-aligned modules (public / admin / user-auth) mirror the existing `surfaces/` tree; a finer per-feature split would further isolate (e.g., separate billing admin from commerce admin) but is premature without a clear re-use signal.

options.label: Three surface-aligned modules: publicRoutes, adminRoutes, userAuthRoutes
options.rationale: Mirrors the existing `surfaces/` directory structure, keeps App under ~40 lines, and is the minimum that satisfies the 'shrink the god entrypoint' goal without over-engineering.

options.label: Per-surface + per-feature split (e.g., adminBillingRoutes, adminCommerceRoutes)
options.rationale: More isolation but requires deciding feature boundaries inside admin; risks creating thin modules and widening the diff with low architectural value right now.

options.label: Single routes module
options.rationale: Only marginally better than today — still centralizes route assembly in one file.

items.context: Docs health reports 6 missing internal docs: `assumptions`, `coherence-notes`, `error-semantics`, `invariants`, `security-posture`, `temporal-flows`. Reaching `health_score >= 0.95` likely requires creating most of them. The `documentation-health` skill lists SEAMS/PROBLEMS/PROGRESS as always-create and the rest as conditional on scenario characteristics (this scenario has React UI + user-facing errors + auth + async flows, so most apply).

options.label: Create all 6 missing docs using `knowledge-observatory docs template` starters
options.rationale: Cleanest path to >=0.95 health and to the scenario's actual needs (React UI → coherence-notes; auth → security-posture; user-facing errors → error-semantics; async AI gateway → temporal-flows; invariants/assumptions are always useful). Docs start as template scaffolds, filled incrementally.

options.label: Create only mandatory subset (invariants, error-semantics, security-posture, coherence-notes) — skip assumptions + temporal-flows
options.rationale: Smaller doc diff; may still hit >=0.95 depending on how docs health weights missing docs. Risks leaving real gaps (async patterns, implicit assumptions).

options.label: Create all 6 as stubs with explicit 'to-be-written' TODOs
options.rationale: Satisfies the manifest/health check quickly but leaves content gaps for future work. Least effort, lowest content value.

items.context: Docs health flags one extra (`docs/FAQ.md`) and two temporary (`docs/plans/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `support-agent-docs/06-email-templates.md`). `FAQ.md` is user-facing content; the others look like scratch artifacts.

options.label: Move FAQ to `docs/guides/faq.md` and register in manifest; delete both temporary docs
options.rationale: FAQ has real user value — promote it into the standard layout. The two temporary docs are scratch/plan artifacts that should not live in the scenario repo. This path maximizes the docs-health score while preserving intent.

options.label: Delete FAQ + both temporaries
options.rationale: Fastest path to a clean health report, but loses FAQ content without verifying it is captured elsewhere.

options.label: Leave FAQ where it is and delete only the two temporaries
options.rationale: Keeps FAQ content intact but extra-doc warning persists (health still penalized, though less than temporary).
